summary: The enterprise AI model API landscape in 2026 is dominated by hyperscaler aggregators — AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI/Foundry, and Google Vertex AI Model Garden — each offering multiple foundation models behind a single managed API that keeps data within the corporation's cloud boundary. There is no single winner; the best fit is driven by an enterprise's existing cloud footprint, required model selection, and compliance needs. Data-platform-native players like Snowflake Cortex AI and governance-focused vendors like IBM watsonx are gaining ground by running models directly against governed enterprise data.
why_enterprises_use_aggregators: Data residency and privacy: prompts, completions, and fine-tuning data stay inside the enterprise's own cloud environment (VPC/region) and are not used to train the vendor's base models.
Compliance and governance: aggregators ship with audit logging, access controls, and certifications (SOC 2, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FedRAMP) that raw vendor APIs often lack out of the box.
Single billing and consolidated contracts: AI spend rolls into existing cloud commitments (EDPs, MACC, committed-use discounts) instead of separate vendor invoices.
Leverage existing cloud footprint: identity (IAM/Entra), networking, security tooling, and data gravity already live in the cloud, so adding models there minimizes integration work.
Model optionality and vendor insurance: one API gives access to many models (Claude, Llama, Mistral, Gemini, Nova, GPT), reducing lock-in and enabling price/performance switching.

platforms.name: Amazon Bedrock
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token (on-demand) plus Provisioned Throughput reserved capacity; batch and import options available.
key_features: No customer data used to train base models
platforms.best_for: Enterprises already on AWS or wanting the widest third-party model choice behind one API.

platforms.name: Azure OpenAI Service / Microsoft Foundry
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token (standard) plus Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) for reserved capacity; included in Azure consumption/MACC.
key_features: Deep integration with Microsoft 365/Copilot and Entra ID
Data not used to train OpenAI models
platforms.best_for: Microsoft-first enterprises wanting first-party OpenAI models with Azure security and identity.

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI Model Garden
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token on-demand plus Provisioned Throughput sold in GSUs (Generative AI Scale Units); ~25 GSUs of Gemini 2.5 Flash ≈ 67,250 tokens/sec sustained.
key_features: Data not used to train base models
platforms.best_for: Data/ML-heavy enterprises on Google Cloud wanting Gemini plus multi-model choice and strong MLOps.

platforms.name: Snowflake Cortex AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based using Snowflake credits (per-token / per-function billing) within existing Snowflake contract.
key_features: Models run directly on governed data inside Snowflake
No data movement outside the platform
platforms.best_for: Enterprises whose data already lives in Snowflake and want governed AI directly on that data.

platforms.name: IBM watsonx.ai
available_models: Third-party and open-source foundation models via catalog
platforms.pricing: Capacity Unit Hours (CUH) and per-token consumption; available as SaaS or on-prem/hybrid via Cloud Pak for Data.
key_features: watsonx.governance for model lifecycle and risk
Named a Leader in 2026 Gartner MQ for DSML Platforms
platforms.best_for: Regulated enterprises needing governance, hybrid/on-prem deployment, and IP indemnification.

platforms.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-use measured in 'Neurons' (compute units); generous free tier, serverless billing.
key_features: Serverless edge inference close to users
AI Gateway for caching, rate-limiting, logging, and analytics
Data Localization Suite for regional residency
Vectorize vector DB and R2 integration
platforms.best_for: Developers and enterprises needing low-latency, serverless, open-model inference at the edge.

platforms.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI
platforms.pricing: On-demand per-character/token pricing plus dedicated AI clusters for reserved capacity.
key_features: Integration with Oracle Fusion/EBS and Autonomous Database
Sovereign cloud and distributed cloud regions
platforms.best_for: Oracle-centric enterprises and sovereign/regulated workloads needing dedicated capacity.

platforms.name: Databricks Mosaic AI / Foundation Model APIs
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based (DBUs) with pay-per-token and provisioned throughput options.
key_features: Models run on governed lakehouse data
Mosaic AI Gateway for routing and audit
platforms.best_for: Data-engineering and ML teams on the Databricks lakehouse wanting governed AI on their data.
